traits.label: Overview
traits.text: Recognizable by its utricular sporangia, the Badhamia utricularis slime mold can be found on rotting wood and leaves. Its lifecycle is captivating, shifting from amoeba-like cells, grouping to form a slug-like mass, and eventually becoming the fruiting body. As a decomposer, it helps recycle nutrients in forest ecosystems, and its distinct sporangia offer a fascinating study for mycologists and naturalists alike.
